title: `str.reverse` reverses grapheme clusters
verdict: graphemes, where the reference reverses code points
description: `str.reverse` reverses extended grapheme clusters (`unicode_reverse`): a letter keeps its combining accent (`e\u0301x` becomes `xe\u0301`) and a flag's two regional indicators stay together. It agrees with the reference on ASCII and on precomposed text.
reference: `reverse` reverses the code points (`String.toList.reverse`), so a combining accent moves to the other side of its letter.

provenance.notes: `sverify_dev.probe_polars` runs each expression on edge cases (0, ±1, ±2, 3, ±7, the bounds of the integer width; 0.5, ±2.5, 7, 1e308, ±inf, NaN; NULL), one row at a time, and compares each row with Lean's outcome of the Substrait call under each candidate option (`substrait-check --outcomes`). Observations are Polars programs whose result is recorded as it is. Polars 2.1.0 (Python), Rust crates at tag py-2.1.0 (commit 7f902bd3), on macOS arm64.
